title: Claude API and SDK Workflows
summary: This intermediate module teaches a repeatable workflow for choosing between direct Claude API access and an SDK, preparing a request, evaluating the response, and handling failures. After completing it, a learner can plan and review a Claude integration workflow that they could not systematically evaluate before.
objectives: Choose between direct API access and an SDK based on the needs of an integration.
Describe the stages of a Claude request from input preparation through response validation.
Apply basic credential, error-handling, and response-review practices to a Claude integration.
Identify what changed in this module's citation record and what the correction affected.

sections.title: What changed in this update
paragraphs: The previous citation was the internal file content/modules/anthropic-claude-practice/claude-api-and-sdk-workflows.json, identified in the supplied review record as an unregistered publisher source that had never been verified. This update replaces that citation with public Anthropic documentation available over HTTPS.

The correction affects source provenance, URL accessibility, publisher attribution, and review metadata. The workflow guidance in this module is limited to claims supported by the replacement sources.
sections.callout: The next review is governed by the module's declared review cadence. A future review should confirm that the cited pages still resolve and that the described workflow still matches Anthropic's documentation.

sections.title: Level and expected background
paragraphs: This is an intermediate module. It assumes that the learner already understands the general client-server pattern in which software sends a request and receives a response.

It also assumes familiarity with structured request data, authentication credentials, and ordinary application error handling. No catalogue prerequisite is declared because no specific existing module was established by the supplied material.

sections.title: Choose direct API access or an SDK
paragraphs: Direct API access gives an application explicit responsibility for constructing requests, supplying authentication, transmitting data, and interpreting responses. This can be appropriate when an application needs close control over its transport and request handling.

An SDK provides a language-oriented client interface around API operations. It can reduce repetitive request and response handling, while the application remains responsible for supplying valid inputs, protecting credentials, interpreting results, and responding to failures.
Choose deliberately. Prefer direct access when transport-level control is important. Prefer an SDK when its supported client interface fits the application and reduces unnecessary integration work.

sections.title: Use a repeatable request workflow
paragraphs: Begin by defining the task and the response your application needs. Prepare the input with enough context and instruction for that task, then select either direct API access or an SDK as the delivery path.

Supply the required authentication through the chosen interface without embedding a secret in material intended for publication or source control. Send the request, retain the operational context needed to diagnose a failure, and distinguish a successful response from an error before consuming returned content.

After a successful response, validate that the returned content is suitable for the application's next step. A technically successful request does not by itself establish that the content is accurate, complete, safe, or appropriate for the intended use.
sections.callout: Treat model output as input to be reviewed and validated, not as automatically trusted application data.

sections.title: Handle failures deliberately
paragraphs: When a request fails, preserve the available error details and determine whether the problem concerns the request, authentication, service availability, or application handling. Correct a request or authentication problem before repeating the same operation.
Do not repeat every failed request without classification. Repetition cannot repair invalid input or missing authorization, and uncontrolled repetition can make an incident harder to diagnose.

Keep integration logic separated into preparation, submission, error classification, and response validation stages. This separation makes it easier to locate a fault and to change the delivery interface without confusing transport behavior with task design.

sections.title: Review the complete workflow
paragraphs: A reviewable Claude workflow has a defined task, an intentional interface choice, protected authentication, a clear request path, explicit success and failure handling, and validation before returned content affects another system or a user.

A learner completing this module can now trace those stages, explain why each exists, and identify where an integration needs stronger handling. Exact implementation details should be taken from the cited Anthropic documentation when the workflow is implemented.

questions.prompt: Which consideration best supports choosing an SDK in the workflow described by this module?
choices: Its supported client interface fits the application and reduces repetitive integration work.
It allows authentication credentials to be published safely.
It guarantees that returned content is accurate.
questions.explanation: The module says an SDK can reduce repetitive request and response handling when its client interface fits the application. It does not remove authentication, validation, or review responsibilities.

questions.prompt: What should happen before returned content affects another system or a user?
choices: The content should be validated for the intended use.
The same request should always be sent again.
The authentication credential should be added to the output.
All error details should be discarded.
questions.explanation: The module requires validation before returned content is used by another system or presented to a user.

questions.prompt: According to the module, what is the first useful response to a failed request?
choices: Classify the problem using the available error details.
Assume the returned content is valid.
Publish the authentication credential for diagnosis.
questions.explanation: The failure-handling section says to preserve error details and determine whether the problem concerns the request, authentication, service availability, or application handling.

questions.prompt: What did the citation correction in this update affect?
choices: Source provenance, URL accessibility, publisher attribution, and review metadata.
A guarantee that model output is accurate.
questions.explanation: The update section explicitly identifies provenance, accessibility, attribution, and review metadata as the effects of replacing the unverified internal citation with public Anthropic documentation.
